blocks.content: PFRDA regulates the National Pension System and administers Atal Pension Yojana to ensure old-age income security.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: PFRDA was initially set up by an executive order in 2003 and attained statutory status via the PFRDA Act, 2013.
It serves as the primary regulatory body overseeing the orderly growth and regulation of the pension market in India.
PFRDA supervises the National Pension System (NPS) and oversees the Atal Pension Yojana (APY) for unorganized workers.
The authority aims to protect subscriber interests and promote long-term old-age income security.
The PFRDA Act was passed in 2013, establishing PFRDA as an autonomous statutory regulatory authority.
NPS was made mandatory for central government employees joining service on or after January 1, 2004 (excluding Armed Forces).
APY is available to Indian citizens in the unorganized sector aged between 18 and 40 years.
